data.body_html:
June is arguably the best month for a Marbella yacht charter weather June offers near-perfect conditions: 29°C air, 22°C sea, and 12 hours of daily sunshine. With only 2 rainy days on average and light winds, you can count on smooth cruising from Puerto Banús. Whether you're planning a sunset cruise or a full-day island hop, this guide breaks down the numbers and the boats that suit the season.

June Weather in Marbella: The Numbers

Average high: 29°C (84°F). Average low: 21°C (70°F). Sea temperature: 22°C (72°F). Sunshine: 12 hours per day. Rain: 2 days total. Wind: 5–10 knots, mostly from the west. These stats come from historic AEMET data and hold steady year after year. The Poniente wind keeps the sea calm, so you won't face choppy conditions.

Sea Temperature: When to Swim

In early June the sea is around 20–21°C; by late June it reaches 22–23°C. Most guests find this comfortable for swimming, especially after a few hours in the sun. Popular anchorages like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés offer clear, calm water. If you prefer warmer water, head to Cabopino – the shallow coves heat up faster.

Best Boats for June Charters

Your choice depends on group size and budget. For small groups (up to 5), the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) are agile and affordable. For 10–12 guests, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) and Mangusta 80 (24m) offer plenty of deck space. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) is a solid mid-range option at €749 for 2 hours. All depart from Puerto Banús.

Pricing & Inclusions

Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours, rising to €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) costs €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter and includes a free jet ski. All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% IVA. No hidden extras.

Where to Cruise in June

From Puerto Banús, head west to Estepona (8 NM) or east to Marbella Marina (3 NM). For lunch stops, Sotogrande (20 NM) offers upscale dining. For swimming, anchor at Río Verde or La Concha viewpoint. The long daylight hours (sunset around 21:30) let you enjoy a full 8-hour charter without rushing.

What to Wear & Bring

Pack sunscreen (SPF 50+), a light jacket for evening, and swimwear. The boat provides towels and snorkelling gear on request. Sunglasses with polarised lenses help reduce glare. A hat is essential – the sun is strong even at 5 PM.

Booking Tips for June

June is high season. Book at least 2–3 weeks in advance, especially for larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86. For last-minute availability, message us on WhatsApp. If you're flexible, a weekday charter (Monday–Thursday) often has more options.

Why June Beats July & August

June offers lower humidity, fewer crowds, and slightly cooler evenings than July/August. The sea is warm enough for swimming but not overcrowded. You'll find more availability and often better pricing. It's the sweet spot for a Marbella yacht charter.
